hypothesis: Requests249-252 show that first-HOT features can rank relative outcomes, but the immediate first-WATCH policy is structurally negative. A precommitted causal pullback/rebound entry rule may convert the ranking signal into positive economics without hindsight-best entry selection.

entry_rules.pullback_1: first observed event at least 1% below the running post-HOT high
entry_rules.pullback_2: first observed event at least 2% below the running post-HOT high
entry_rules.pullback_3: first observed event at least 3% below the running post-HOT high
entry_rules.rebound_2_1: after a >=2% pullback from the running high, enter on the first >=1% rebound from the post-pullback low

exit_value: equal-weight BASE return to the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 5th subsequently observed events after entry, all inside the 30-minute risk cap
forbidden: choosing the best future entry event
changing pullback thresholds after reading May outcomes
opening June15-19 unless a May rule passes
next_if_pass: Freeze candidate threshold and causal entry rule, then open June15-19 as a new holdout.
next_if_fail: Simple causal waiting cannot rescue the fixed-policy economics; redesign the candidate/state representation or learn a richer causal entry state before any new holdout.
